facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage is moderate and its direction is flat to slightly worse. Gross debt at carrying value fell by only USD 2.449 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell below the fiscal 2025 figure, because sales and marketing and product development spending rose by more than the whole increase in revenue in the first half of 2026. For creditors this means deleveraging is coming from debt paydown that is too small to matter, not from earnings growth, so the reported ratio has edged up from 4.14x to 4.22x even though the issuer's adjusted ratio looks lower. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: The gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is entirely three issuer add-backs. Stock-based compensation recurs in every period and is a real economic cost, because the company issues shares to staff and spends cash on repurchases, which adjusted EBITDA ignores. The transaction-related and other non-recurring line has been present in every year shown, which means its non-recurring character is not established, and the issuer gives no component split. A creditor should therefore anchor on the reported ratio and treat the adjusted ratio as an upper bound on earnings quality, not as a covenant calculation. Basis: calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: The strongest offset is cash generation and a small, simple capital structure. Free cash flow after cash interest and capital spending was positive in every period shown, and a single term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.500 million a year leaves no refinancing event before the 2031 balloon. The offset is weakened by capital allocation: fiscal 2025 repurchases exceeded free cash flow, and cash fell even with disposal proceeds. First-half 2026 repurchases were covered by free cash flow, so the observable test is whether that holds as earnings soften. Cash flow figures are consolidated and still include the sold marketing business, so they overstate continuing cash generation to an extent the filings do not quantify. Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate and not the near-term constraint. Cash at June 30, 2026 plus the undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, is the only liquidity the filings establish; USD 30.0 million of the commitments expired on July 6, 2026, a dated later event that is not blended into the period figure. The revolver carries a springing first lien leverage test that applies only if more than 35% of commitments are drawn, nothing is drawn, and the reported ratio is not stated, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated from these tables. Interest rate protection is a second watch item: swaps cover most of the term loan only until October 31, 2027, after which the whole loan floats, while the issuer's own sensitivity today is small. facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: A supported downside sequence starts with weaker retention: the annualized net revenue retention rate was about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 against about 97% a year earlier, and pro forma revenue growth in that quarter was 2.0%. Slower growth against rising sales and product spending would first compress EBITDA, which raises leverage on a debt balance that barely amortizes; cash and the undrawn revolver would then absorb any shortfall, with repurchases the discretionary outflow. Observable triggers are net revenue retention, the guidance range for adjusted EBITDA, buybacks against free cash flow and any revolver draw. No numerical stress or runway is established here. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C13; calculation C10

rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: The issuer reports a material weakness over order-to-cash revenue accounting that was not remediated at December 31, 2025, and its disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026. The audited annual statements are unqualified and the issuer states no misstatement, but revenue, receivables and deferred revenue carry a reliability discount until remediation is reported. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56 - Medium: The first lien leverage ratio the issuer reports against its revolver covenant, the covenant definitions and the credit agreement are not supplied. Covenant headroom and add-back eligibility are therefore not calculable from these statements, and the ratios above are not covenant calculations. The relative lien priority of the term loan and the revolver is also not stated; both are shown at the first rank because the issuer tests a first lien leverage ratio and discloses no other debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 208–209 - Medium: The cash flow statements are consolidated and include the marketing technology business until October 31, 2025, with no continuing-operations split, so free cash flow, cash conversion and the last-twelve-month cash flow proxies are not on the same perimeter as EBITDA. A continuing-operations cash flow would close the gap. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160 - Low: Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not stated in any supplied document, so undrawn availability net of them is not established and the liquidity table is gross of them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54 - Low: No document covers a period after June 30, 2026, so current leverage, liquidity and covenant position after the second quarter are not established and no event after that date changes net debt in the sources. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C09 - Low: Source dashes are kept as missing, not zero: loss on sale and impairments in three quarters, discontinued operations in 2026 periods, and several cash flow lines. Totals stay usable and each dash is not certified as zero. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160 - Low: Revenue by vertical, a business-unit EBITDA split, maintenance against growth capital spending and the fourth quarter of 2025 cash flow are not disclosed, so no segment sum or quarterly cash flow is stated. The single reportable segment equals the consolidated totals. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 202

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the sponsors' conduct on the record: no dividend has ever been paid, the only shareholder payments are cash-funded share repurchases, and the 2024 and 2025 amendments pushed the term loan to July 2031 and lowered its margin. A business with hundreds of thousands of customers and recurring revenue can absorb slower growth without a funding event. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: A second counterpoint to the diversification finding is the issuer's own warning of key customers and more concentration in certain markets, which the filings do not size; a disclosed share above a tenth of revenue would weaken that finding. The view would improve if the control weakness is reported remediated, if retention and growth recover, and if the proxy statement and credit agreement show no related-party fees or distribution capacity beyond what the filings describe. It would worsen if the chief executive change proves disorderly, if the sponsors sell down or the board approves a debt-funded payment to shareholders, or if buybacks again exceed the cash the business generates. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No new debt was issued in the period read. The company repriced and extended its term loan and revolver three times: an amendment on December 13, 2024 cut the margin and removed the credit spread adjustment; one on June 10, 2025 reduced the revolver to USD 155.0 million and extended USD 125.0 million of it; and one on July 29, 2025 pushed the term loan maturity to July 6, 2031 and the extended revolver to July 29, 2030. For creditors this removed any maturity before 2030 and lowered cash interest, and it shows lenders were willing to extend. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue durability is average: the base is broad and mostly recurring, but customers can leave quickly. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so no single customer failure moves cash flow, yet most contracts are open-ended and can be ended on 30 days' notice. Annualized net revenue retention slipped to about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 from about 97% a year earlier, so the installed base is shrinking before new sales and price increases, and growth now depends on selling more and charging more. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Key findings

facts.text: Governance is the weakest dimension, and the weakness is about information and control rather than documented creditor harm. Two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the shares and must consent to a change of control, to deals above USD 500.0 million and to chief executive changes while together at 30% or more; the revenue-accounting control weakness has been reported in three annual reports and disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026; and the latest release refers to a new chief executive without detail. facts.label: Financial profile
facts.text: The nine-dimension view is as follows. Scale and market position is average: last-twelve-month revenue of USD 598.10 million in fragmented markets with low barriers to entry. Competitive advantage is average: integrated vertical workflows raise switching costs, but most contracts end on 30 days' notice and retention is slipping. Business diversification is strong: customers are dispersed across home, health and wellness services and 88.79% of first-half 2026 revenue is from the United States, which limits currency exposure. Cost and capex flexibility is average: sales, marketing and product development are 36.53% of first-half revenue and can be slowed, but rent, salaries and debt service are fixed or semi-fixed. Margin stability is average: gross margin is steady and the EBITDA margin is falling. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in every period but on a perimeter that still includes the sold business. Ability to refinance is average: three amendments show access, but 95.28% of the principal is one 2031 bullet in a sponsor-controlled company. Liquidity is strong on stated figures at USD 258.50 million against USD 33.11 million of last-twelve-month cash interest, before letters of credit. Financial policy and governance is weak: concentrated control, a persistent control weakness and buybacks above free cash flow after amortization, offset by no dividend ever paid. facts.label: Business model and ownership
facts.text: EverCommerce sells vertically tailored software to service small and medium businesses in home, health and wellness services, bundling business management, billing and payments and customer-experience tools in one segment. Revenue visibility comes from subscription and transaction fees, 96.27% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and the cash-generation mechanism is simple: recurring fees on a dispersed base funded from a low-capital-intensity model. Ownership is concentrated in two sponsors that hold about 85.7% of the shares, so the credit depends on their financial policy rather than on public-market discipline; the filings name no parent, and the creditors' claim sits on the operating group through subsidiary guarantees and pledged equity under the credit facilities. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C08; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Revenue, cost and cash conversion
facts.text: Revenue is predictable and recurring but not contractually locked. Business management software drove a USD 9.5 million rise in first-half subscription and transaction revenue, mainly through higher revenue per customer, billing and payment solutions added USD 0.8 million on volume and a slightly higher take rate, and rebates from group purchasing fell USD 1.4 million. Payments are about 20% of revenue and depend on card networks and processors, so a pricing-led increase combined with falling retention makes revenue more sensitive to churn and to small-business spending than the recurring label suggests. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 35–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53

facts.label: Revenue, cost and cash conversion
facts.text: Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if discretionary spending is slowed. Cost of revenues is steady, but sales and marketing rose 12.49% and product development 7.94% in the first half, and the increase over the prior-year spending ratio is worth about USD 7.42 million per half-year, or 8.44% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA when annualized. That is a real management lever, but pulling it trades near-term EBITDA for slower growth in a business where retention is already weakening. Basis: calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

facts.text: Cash conversion is good before shareholder returns. Free cash flow before cash interest was 84.82% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and 59.60% of Adjusted EBITDA; the gap to the adjusted figure reflects capital spending, taxes and the transaction-related costs that the issuer adds back but pays in cash, which makes the adjusted measure a poor guide to cash. facts.label: Claims outside the debt figure
facts.text: The claims outside the debt figure are small against cash generation. Operating lease liabilities of USD 12.01 million, USD 13.24 million undiscounted with a weighted remaining term of 3.89 years, sit outside debt and their cost is already inside EBITDA; non-cancelable purchase obligations for software services, mail, fulfilment and hosting total USD 31.97 million to 2029; and up to USD 6.5 million of ZyraTalk contingent consideration may be paid over three years. Together the leases and purchase obligations are USD 43.98 million, less than one year of free cash flow. The company has no finance leases and the sources read show no pensions, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance, and the Delaware class action carries no accrual because a loss is not probable or estimable. facts.label: Competitive and external forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high and caps pricing. The issuer competes with manual processes, vertical specialists and horizontal vendors including Salesforce, Intuit and Square, and describes barriers to entry as generally low, so spending to defend retention is structural and margin gains are hard to hold. New entrants and substitutes work through the same mechanism: the filings expect more entrants and name partners that may become competitors, and the analyst view is that AI-native tools are a further substitute the filings do not size, so each raises the sales and product spending needed to keep revenue per customer rising. Buyer power is individually weak but collectively strong, because small customers can leave on 30 days' notice and are price-sensitive in a downturn. Supplier power is moderate: card networks and payment processors sit between the company and about 20% of its revenue and can fine or terminate it for non-compliance. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53

facts.label: Competitive and external forces
facts.text: Economic and regulatory factors are material to credit; currency and politics are not. A weaker economy could close small businesses at higher rates, shrink card volumes and slow spending on software, and the company says fixed and semi-fixed costs including debt service cannot be cut quickly; interest-rate rises matter through the floating-rate term loan. Payment-network rules, data-privacy law and AI regulation raise compliance cost but are not quantified in the filings, and international revenue is 11.21% of the first half, so currency is minor. facts.label: Competitive and external forces
facts.text: The credit-translated SWOT is as follows. Strengths are dispersed recurring revenue, a stable gross margin, a long simple capital structure and positive free cash flow. Weaknesses are slipping retention, add-back-heavy earnings, a persistent control weakness and repurchases above free cash flow after amortization. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are payments cross-selling and AI products raising revenue per customer, remediation of the control weakness and holding repurchases inside free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are a small-business downturn, price competition from low-barrier entrants, rising rates after the swaps expire and a sponsor sell-down or disorderly chief executive change. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C07

facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer's own guidance and the swap expiry set the picture. Management expects results toward the lower end of ranges that were unchanged since March, quarterly results have so far met or beaten their ranges, and no maturity falls due beyond USD 5.50 million of amortization a year; headwinds are retention near 94%, spending that outruns revenue, the dilutive ZyraTalk purchase and the October 2027 swap expiry. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside begins with the customer base, not a lender event. A soft economy closes small businesses and cuts card volumes while retention, already near 94%, slips further and contracts end on 30 days' notice, so revenue growth stalls; because spending is rising 10.67% and rent, salaries and debt service are semi-fixed, EBITDA falls faster than revenue. Each USD 10.0 million of lost last-twelve-month reported EBITDA lifts gross leverage from 4.22x to 4.59x and lowers reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.43x, and the pressure compounds if floating-rate cost rises after October 2027. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58

facts.text: Liquidity would absorb the shock before covenants or maturities matter. With free cash flow of USD 71.69 million and cash of USD 133.50 million, only a revolver draw above 35% of commitments, which is USD 43.75 million, would start the first lien leverage test of 7.50x; with zero operating cash flow, cash alone would meet cash interest and amortization for 3.46 years and cash plus the full revolver, if it stayed available, for 6.70 years. The levers are suspending buybacks of USD 82.11 million a year, slowing spending by about USD 7.42 million per half-year and capitalized software of USD 15.58 million per half-year, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within two years; the exposure is the 2030 to 2031 refinancing if EBITDA is lower by then. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, EverCommerce presents an adequate business profile supported by dispersed recurring revenue and a stable gross margin, but credit quality is constrained by slowing growth, add-back-heavy earnings and sponsor-controlled governance with a weak reporting record. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers scheduled amortization 13.03x, although it does not cover buybacks on top. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilizing before the revolver matures in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031, and on lenders' continued appetite. The primary downside path is weaker retention and spending that outruns revenue pressing EBITDA and leverage while repurchases continue. The profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set was supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer benchmarks and the filings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Top risk: retention-led earnings erosion ahead of a 2031 bullet refinancing. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for EverCommerce Inc. (issuer evcm), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the seven supplied filings and earnings releases can support the requested financial foundation, business and governance and fundamental credit work, and what is missing. No credit conclusion is drawn here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Source coverage is sufficient for a credit snapshot through the quarter ended June 30, 2026, but covenant, security and control conclusions are limited by missing legal documents and an unremediated weakness in revenue-accounting controls.

Four discrete quarters, the audited 2025 statements and the debt note tie to one another on one consolidated perimeter, so leverage, coverage and liquidity work can proceed. The credit agreement, the terms of the chief executive transition, the letters of credit issued under the revolver and every period after June 30, 2026 are missing from the set. The main contrary point is that the filings report covenant compliance and no revolver borrowings, so these gaps limit confirmation of protections rather than signal stress. Supplying the credit agreement and the filings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 would resolve the covenant, security and timeliness limits.

## Findings
### Bottom line

EverCommerce's single secured term loan is serviceable but less lightly levered than the issuer's adjusted figures suggest: gross debt is 4.22x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at June 30, 2026, against 2.96x on the adjusted measure, and the balloon is not due until 2031.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

Net debt is 3.14x reported EBITDA and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.73x, so servicing is comfortable on cash figures the issuer itself reports. The adjusted ratios rest on USD 52.28 million of add-backs, mostly stock compensation and one-off costs, and adjusted EBITDA has slipped below the fiscal 2025 level as management guides to the low end of its range. The main contrary point is an undrawn revolver and no balloon before 2031, which limits refinancing pressure. The view would worsen if adjusted EBITDA keeps falling or if buybacks again exceed free cash flow.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C07; calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54

### Financial interpretation

Leverage is moderate and its direction is flat to slightly worse. Gross debt at carrying value fell by only USD 2.449 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell below the fiscal 2025 figure, because sales and marketing and product development spending rose by more than the whole increase in revenue in the first half of 2026. For creditors this means deleveraging is coming from debt paydown that is too small to matter, not from earnings growth, so the reported ratio has edged up from 4.14x to 4.22x even though the issuer's adjusted ratio looks lower.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6

The gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is entirely three issuer add-backs. Stock-based compensation recurs in every period and is a real economic cost, because the company issues shares to staff and spends cash on repurchases, which adjusted EBITDA ignores. The transaction-related and other non-recurring line has been present in every year shown, which means its non-recurring character is not established, and the issuer gives no component split. A creditor should therefore anchor on the reported ratio and treat the adjusted ratio as an upper bound on earnings quality, not as a covenant calculation.
Basis: calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

The strongest offset is cash generation and a small, simple capital structure. Free cash flow after cash interest and capital spending was positive in every period shown, and a single term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.500 million a year leaves no refinancing event before the 2031 balloon. The offset is weakened by capital allocation: fiscal 2025 repurchases exceeded free cash flow, and cash fell even with disposal proceeds. First-half 2026 repurchases were covered by free cash flow, so the observable test is whether that holds as earnings soften. Cash flow figures are consolidated and still include the sold marketing business, so they overstate continuing cash generation to an extent the filings do not quantify.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

Liquidity is adequate and not the near-term constraint. Cash at June 30, 2026 plus the undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, is the only liquidity the filings establish; USD 30.0 million of the commitments expired on July 6, 2026, a dated later event that is not blended into the period figure. The revolver carries a springing first lien leverage test that applies only if more than 35% of commitments are drawn, nothing is drawn, and the reported ratio is not stated, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated from these tables. Interest rate protection is a second watch item: swaps cover most of the term loan only until October 31, 2027, after which the whole loan floats, while the issuer's own sensitivity today is small.
Basis: calculation C09; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156

Customer deposits and deferred revenue are a non-debt funding source and not ordinary payables. Together they stand at about USD 35.152 million and have grown slowly from December 2024, so customers prepay for services the company must still deliver. A drop in billings would remove this float before revenue falls, which makes these two lines an early indicator to monitor alongside net revenue retention.
Basis: calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158

A supported downside sequence starts with weaker retention: the annualized net revenue retention rate was about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 against about 97% a year earlier, and pro forma revenue growth in that quarter was 2.0%. Slower growth against rising sales and product spending would first compress EBITDA, which raises leverage on a debt balance that barely amortizes; cash and the undrawn revolver would then absorb any shortfall, with repurchases the discretionary outflow. Observable triggers are net revenue retention, the guidance range for adjusted EBITDA, buybacks against free cash flow and any revolver draw. No numerical stress or runway is established here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C13; calculation C10

### Limitations

The statements are consolidated figures in thousands of US dollars, converted to millions only in the money tables. The issuer states only an adjusted EBITDA, so the reported measure used for leverage and cover is calculated from operating income and depreciation and amortization and is unadjusted. Last-twelve-month figures are constructed from a fiscal year and two half-years and tie to the sum of four reported quarters. The latest period is the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and nothing later was available.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6

The cash flow statements include the marketing technology business until its sale on October 31, 2025, while the income statement shows it as discontinued operations, so cash conversion is not on the same perimeter as EBITDA. The issuer reports an unremediated material weakness over revenue accounting controls, and its disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026; the annual statements carry an unqualified audit opinion, but internal control is not audited. Covenant definitions, the reported first lien leverage ratio and letters of credit issued under the revolver are not established because the credit agreement is not supplied.

- High: The issuer reports a material weakness over order-to-cash revenue accounting that was not remediated at December 31, 2025, and its disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026. The audited annual statements are unqualified and the issuer states no misstatement, but revenue, receivables and deferred revenue carry a reliability discount until remediation is reported.

- Medium: The first lien leverage ratio the issuer reports against its revolver covenant, the covenant definitions and the credit agreement are not supplied. Covenant headroom and add-back eligibility are therefore not calculable from these statements, and the ratios above are not covenant calculations. The relative lien priority of the term loan and the revolver is also not stated; both are shown at the first rank because the issuer tests a first lien leverage ratio and discloses no other debt.

- Medium: The cash flow statements are consolidated and include the marketing technology business until October 31, 2025, with no continuing-operations split, so free cash flow, cash conversion and the last-twelve-month cash flow proxies are not on the same perimeter as EBITDA. A continuing-operations cash flow would close the gap.

- Low: Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not stated in any supplied document, so undrawn availability net of them is not established and the liquidity table is gross of them.

- Low: No document covers a period after June 30, 2026, so current leverage, liquidity and covenant position after the second quarter are not established and no event after that date changes net debt in the sources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C09

- Low: Source dashes are kept as missing, not zero: loss on sale and impairments in three quarters, discontinued operations in 2026 periods, and several cash flow lines. Totals stay usable and each dash is not certified as zero.

- Low: Revenue by vertical, a business-unit EBITDA split, maintenance against growth capital spending and the fourth quarter of 2025 cash flow are not disclosed, so no segment sum or quarterly cash flow is stated. The single reportable segment equals the consolidated totals.

spans.text: ## Request

Business and governance review of EverCommerce Inc. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, sponsor and governance facts, transactions and capital allocation that matter to a creditor, from the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

EverCommerce is a diversified, mostly recurring small-business software company whose main credit risk is control rather than customers: two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the stock with consent rights over key decisions, while growth is slowing and spending is outrunning revenue.

No sponsor action adverse to creditors is documented: the company has never paid a dividend, its refinancings extended maturities and cut margins, and the latest acquisition was paid in cash. Against that, the issuer reports an unremediated revenue-accounting control weakness and refers to a new chief executive without saying who, when or on what terms, so management continuity is a question, not a finding.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

Revenue is broad and mostly recurring, so near-term cash flow does not depend on a few customers. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025, and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring. The mechanism is dispersion across a large base, which supports debt service at a moderate leverage level. The issuer also warns of key customers and a more pronounced concentration in certain markets without sizing them, so dispersion is established by customer count, not by revenue share.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation C01

Growth is modest and retention is slipping, which is the main operating threat to coverage. Revenue grew 3.2% in the first half of 2026 against 4.8% in fiscal 2025, and annualized net revenue retention was about 94% in the second quarter against about 97% a year earlier. A customer base that sheds revenue faster than it adds it forces more sales spending just to hold earnings steady.

Spending is growing faster than revenue, so the earnings cushion is thinning. In the first half of 2026 sales and marketing rose 12.5% and product development 7.9%, together more than the whole revenue increase, and Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 85.21 million from USD 89.90 million. If revenue growth does not recover, the same spending base erodes cash interest cover before it threatens liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C03

The acquisition programme has slowed and the latest purchase is dilutive in the near term. The company has acquired 54 companies since inception, paid about USD 36.0 million in cash for ZyraTalk in September 2025 with up to USD 6.5 million more contingent over three years, and added no debt to do so. In the first half of 2026 ZyraTalk contributed USD 1.8 million of revenue against USD 5.3 million of post-acquisition operating expense, so it adds to the earnings drag until it scales.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 185; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47; calculation C06

Control sits with two sponsors whose consent rights reach the decisions creditors care about, but no creditor-adverse use of them is documented. While the sponsors together hold at least 30% of the stock they must consent to a change of control, to any acquisition or disposal above USD 500.0 million, to hiring or removing the chief executive and to insolvency filings, and each can nominate directors while it holds at least 5%. This gives them the discretion to change capital policy without creditor consent unless the credit agreement, which is not supplied, restrains it.

Reporting quality is the weakest part of governance. The issuer has disclosed the same revenue-accounting control weakness in its fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports and its disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026. The statements still carry a clean audit opinion, so the risk is that revenue, receivables and deferred revenue are less reliable than their precision suggests.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the sponsors' conduct on the record: no dividend has ever been paid, the only shareholder payments are cash-funded share repurchases, and the 2024 and 2025 amendments pushed the term loan to July 2031 and lowered its margin. A business with hundreds of thousands of customers and recurring revenue can absorb slower growth without a funding event.

A second counterpoint to the diversification finding is the issuer's own warning of key customers and more concentration in certain markets, which the filings do not size; a disclosed share above a tenth of revenue would weaken that finding. The view would improve if the control weakness is reported remediated, if retention and growth recover, and if the proxy statement and credit agreement show no related-party fees or distribution capacity beyond what the filings describe. It would worsen if the chief executive change proves disorderly, if the sponsors sell down or the board approves a debt-funded payment to shareholders, or if buybacks again exceed the cash the business generates.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 208–209
### Limitations

- The proxy statement that holds related-party transactions, sponsor fees, executive pay and each sponsor's individual percentage was not supplied, so the finding that no creditor-adverse sponsor action is documented covers only the annual and quarterly filings and releases read.

- Revenue by vertical, the size of the key customers the issuer warns about and any investor presentation were not supplied, so the diversification finding rests on customer counts and revenue type, not on business-line or customer shares.
- The only reference to a chief executive transition is one sentence in the latest release, so the management-continuity point is an open question and no view is taken on who leads or when.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2
- The credit agreement that limits dividends, investments and asset sales was not supplied, so what the sponsors may do with cash, as opposed to what they have done, is not assessed.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of EverCommerce Inc. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view built on the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases and on the accepted source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses. It gives no rating, legal-capacity conclusion, recovery value or portfolio sizing.
## Sources

No external sources were used. The run settings are not an issuer source and are not listed.
## Findings
### Bottom line

EverCommerce is an adequate credit, not a strong one: recurring, widely spread revenue and a single term loan not due until 2031 support debt service, while slowing growth, add-back-heavy earnings and sponsor control leave little room for error. Gross debt is 4.22x reported EBITDA and 2.96x the issuer's adjusted measure, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.73x, so servicing is comfortable today.
Basis: calculation C01; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main downside path is weaker customer retention and spending that grows faster than revenue eroding earnings while share repurchases continue. Full-year guidance also needs a fourth quarter the company has not yet reported, which tests management's forecasting more than debt service.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Key findings

Revenue durability is average: the base is broad and mostly recurring, but customers can leave quickly. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so no single customer failure moves cash flow, yet most contracts are open-ended and can be ended on 30 days' notice. Annualized net revenue retention slipped to about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 from about 97% a year earlier, so the installed base is shrinking before new sales and price increases, and growth now depends on selling more and charging more.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margins hold at the gross line but erode below it. Gross margin before depreciation and amortization was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 against 77.75% a year earlier, yet sales and marketing together with product development grew 10.67% against revenue growth of 3.17%, and Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.22% to USD 85.21 million. Reported EBITDA is 20.66% of last-twelve-month revenue and Adjusted EBITDA 29.40%; the gap is USD 52.28 million of add-backs, 29.73% of the adjusted figure, so the adjusted ratios flatter the cushion.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash flow covers mandatory debt service many times but not shareholder returns on top of it. Free cash flow after cash interest, taxes and capital spending was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months against scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million, which is 13.03x cover, but cash share repurchases of USD 82.11 million exceeded free cash flow after amortization by USD 15.92 million and were 3.32x the stock compensation expense. Only USD 19.2 million of the authorization remains, though the board has raised it five times, so the buyback is a discretionary draw on liquidity that the board, under sponsor control, can renew.

Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is moderate but not falling, and the term loan is one long bullet. Reported leverage was 4.22x at June 30, 2026 against 4.14x at the end of 2025 and 4.94x at the end of 2024, because last-twelve-month EBITDA slipped while debt fell by only USD 2.45 million in the half. About 95.28% of the principal falls due in July 2031, so repayment rests on refinancing a business whose growth is slowing, helped by lenders having agreed three amendments in 2024 and 2025 that cut margins and pushed maturities out.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 to 2031 question, not a near-term one. Cash of USD 133.50 million plus the undrawn revolver gives USD 258.50 million after USD 30.0 million of commitments expired on July 6, 2026, before any letters of credit, which the filings cap at a USD 20.0 million sub-limit. The only financial test described is a first lien leverage ratio of 7.50x on the revolver, applied only if more than 35% is drawn, so the filings describe no financial maintenance test for the term loan.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Interest-rate protection is partial and temporary. Swaps fix the floating rate on USD 425.0 million, 81.1% of the principal, only until October 31, 2027; each 100 bp rise costs about USD 1.0 million a year now and about USD 5.16 million a year once the swaps expire, which would lower reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.23x on last-twelve-month figures.
Basis: calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156

Full-year guidance looks back-end loaded, which questions management's forecasting more than the debt. Management said in May that it expected growth to accelerate in the second half and in August that its outlook had moderated, yet the March ranges were unchanged: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 183.0 million to USD 191.0 million and revenue of USD 612.0 million to USD 632.0 million, with results now expected toward the lower end. After USD 85.21 million in the first half and a third-quarter range of USD 44.0 million to USD 46.0 million, the low end needs a fourth quarter of at least USD 51.79 million, 17.29% above the fourth quarter of 2025; two quarters at the third-quarter midpoint would give USD 175.21 million, USD 7.79 million short.

Basis: calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

Governance is the weakest dimension, and the weakness is about information and control rather than documented creditor harm. Two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the shares and must consent to a change of control, to deals above USD 500.0 million and to chief executive changes while together at 30% or more; the revenue-accounting control weakness has been reported in three annual reports and disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026; and the latest release refers to a new chief executive without detail. No dividend has ever been paid and no sponsor extraction is documented, but the credit agreement that would show what the sponsors may do with cash was not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is conduct and cash. The 2026 quarterly ranges were met or beaten: first-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 40.67 million sat inside a range of USD 39.0 million to USD 41.0 million and second-quarter USD 44.54 million was above a range of USD 41.0 million to USD 43.0 million. First-half repurchases of USD 28.57 million were covered by free cash flow of USD 36.08 million, free cash flow has been positive in every period reported, no dividend has ever been paid, and adjusted leverage of 2.96x leaves room for earnings to fall before servicing is stressed. Lenders also agreed three amendments that lowered margins and extended maturities, which shows market access.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C09; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; Financial foundation (CP-1)

This view would win if retention stabilizes near 97%, discretionary spending growth fades toward revenue growth so that EBITDA stops falling, and the fourth quarter delivers the step-up the guidance requires; the credit would then rate better than adequate. It would worsen if third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 44.0 million, if the revolver is drawn, if the repurchase authorization is raised again while repurchases exceed free cash flow, if the sponsors sell below 30% or the chief executive change proves disorderly, or if the control weakness is still unremediated in the next annual report.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- No creditor-protection document was supplied, so the conclusion that servicing is comfortable rests on cash flow and not on contractual rights: what the term lenders can enforce, how much the sponsors may distribute and how large any letters of credit are remain unknown, the covenant's own ratio and EBITDA definition are not stated so the leverage ratios here are not covenant calculations, and the liquidity figure stays gross of letters of credit.

- No peer or sector benchmark was supplied, so "adequate" and "moderate" compare the issuer with its own history and with the 7.50x revolver test, not with other leveraged software issuers, and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52

- The back-end loading finding is the analyst's arithmetic on the issuer's published ranges; the issuer gives no quantified bridge to the fourth quarter beyond a May statement that growth should accelerate, so an unannounced price increase, acquisition or timing item could make the ranges reachable and the finding would then fall away.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C02

- The filings do not split revenue growth between price and volume or give retention by customer group beyond one rate, so how much of the weaker retention is controllable cannot be established and the cost-flexibility estimate carries that uncertainty.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C03
### Strengths and weaknesses

Dispersed, mostly recurring revenue is the first strength. About 93% of customers each contributed under USD 2 thousand in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so a customer loss is small and renewals repeat; the consequence for creditors is steadier cash flow at moderate leverage, tempered by the issuer's unsized warning of key customers.

A stable gross margin and some pricing power are the second strength. Gross margin was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 and business management revenue rose USD 9.5 million mainly on higher revenue per customer, so price and mix are offsetting weaker retention for now; if retention keeps slipping, price increases become the main lever and carry churn risk.
Basis: calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45

A simple, long-dated capital structure is the third strength. One term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million a year and an undrawn revolver to July 2030 leave no maturity wall before 2030, so refinancing depends on earnings in 2029 and 2030, not on the next two years.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

Free cash flow that covers mandatory debt service is the fourth strength. Free cash flow after cash interest was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months, 13.03x scheduled amortization, and capital spending including capitalized software was 5.41% of fiscal 2025 revenue, so cash generation does not depend on heavy reinvestment.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160

Liquidity with no revolver draw is the fifth strength. Cash of USD 133.50 million and USD 125.0 million of undrawn revolver commitments give USD 258.50 million, and customer deposits and deferred revenue of USD 35.15 million are a non-debt source of funding that would shrink if billings fell; the revolver commitment expired in part on July 6, 2026 and is shown after that date.

Governance and reporting reliability are the first weakness. An unremediated revenue-accounting control weakness in three annual reports, controls that were not effective at June 30, 2026 and an unexplained chief executive transition reduce confidence in the figures creditors rely on and in management continuity, while sponsor consent rights let two holders steer capital policy.

### Financial profile

The nine-dimension view is as follows. Scale and market position is average: last-twelve-month revenue of USD 598.10 million in fragmented markets with low barriers to entry. Competitive advantage is average: integrated vertical workflows raise switching costs, but most contracts end on 30 days' notice and retention is slipping. Business diversification is strong: customers are dispersed across home, health and wellness services and 88.79% of first-half 2026 revenue is from the United States, which limits currency exposure. Cost and capex flexibility is average: sales, marketing and product development are 36.53% of first-half revenue and can be slowed, but rent, salaries and debt service are fixed or semi-fixed. Margin stability is average: gross margin is steady and the EBITDA margin is falling. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in every period but on a perimeter that still includes the sold business. Ability to refinance is average: three amendments show access, but 95.28% of the principal is one 2031 bullet in a sponsor-controlled company. Liquidity is strong on stated figures at USD 258.50 million against USD 33.11 million of last-twelve-month cash interest, before letters of credit. Financial policy and governance is weak: concentrated control, a persistent control weakness and buybacks above free cash flow after amortization, offset by no dividend ever paid.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C08; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Business model and ownership

EverCommerce sells vertically tailored software to service small and medium businesses in home, health and wellness services, bundling business management, billing and payments and customer-experience tools in one segment. Revenue visibility comes from subscription and transaction fees, 96.27% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and the cash-generation mechanism is simple: recurring fees on a dispersed base funded from a low-capital-intensity model. Ownership is concentrated in two sponsors that hold about 85.7% of the shares, so the credit depends on their financial policy rather than on public-market discipline; the filings name no parent, and the creditors' claim sits on the operating group through subsidiary guarantees and pledged equity under the credit facilities.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C08; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The roll-up history matters for creditors only through cash and earnings. The company has bought 54 businesses since inception, paid about USD 36.0 million in cash for ZyraTalk in September 2025 with no new debt, and sold its marketing technology business for about USD 45.0 million in cash in October 2025, so acquisitions are now funded from cash and the disposal shrank revenue; ZyraTalk added USD 1.8 million of first-half revenue against USD 5.3 million of operating expense, an early drag on EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue, cost and cash conversion

Revenue is predictable and recurring but not contractually locked. Business management software drove a USD 9.5 million rise in first-half subscription and transaction revenue, mainly through higher revenue per customer, billing and payment solutions added USD 0.8 million on volume and a slightly higher take rate, and rebates from group purchasing fell USD 1.4 million. Payments are about 20% of revenue and depend on card networks and processors, so a pricing-led increase combined with falling retention makes revenue more sensitive to churn and to small-business spending than the recurring label suggests.

Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if discretionary spending is slowed. Cost of revenues is steady, but sales and marketing rose 12.49% and product development 7.94% in the first half, and the increase over the prior-year spending ratio is worth about USD 7.42 million per half-year, or 8.44% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA when annualized. That is a real management lever, but pulling it trades near-term EBITDA for slower growth in a business where retention is already weakening.
Basis: calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

Cash conversion is good before shareholder returns. Free cash flow before cash interest was 84.82% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and 59.60% of Adjusted EBITDA; the gap to the adjusted figure reflects capital spending, taxes and the transaction-related costs that the issuer adds back but pays in cash, which makes the adjusted measure a poor guide to cash. The weakness is the use of that cash, since capitalized software has risen faster than expense and buybacks absorb more than the cash left after amortization.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Claims outside the debt figure

The claims outside the debt figure are small against cash generation. Operating lease liabilities of USD 12.01 million, USD 13.24 million undiscounted with a weighted remaining term of 3.89 years, sit outside debt and their cost is already inside EBITDA; non-cancelable purchase obligations for software services, mail, fulfilment and hosting total USD 31.97 million to 2029; and up to USD 6.5 million of ZyraTalk contingent consideration may be paid over three years. Together the leases and purchase obligations are USD 43.98 million, less than one year of free cash flow. The company has no finance leases and the sources read show no pensions, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance, and the Delaware class action carries no accrual because a loss is not probable or estimable.
### Competitive and external forces

Competitive rivalry is high and caps pricing. The issuer competes with manual processes, vertical specialists and horizontal vendors including Salesforce, Intuit and Square, and describes barriers to entry as generally low, so spending to defend retention is structural and margin gains are hard to hold. New entrants and substitutes work through the same mechanism: the filings expect more entrants and name partners that may become competitors, and the analyst view is that AI-native tools are a further substitute the filings do not size, so each raises the sales and product spending needed to keep revenue per customer rising. Buyer power is individually weak but collectively strong, because small customers can leave on 30 days' notice and are price-sensitive in a downturn. Supplier power is moderate: card networks and payment processors sit between the company and about 20% of its revenue and can fine or terminate it for non-compliance.

Economic and regulatory factors are material to credit; currency and politics are not. A weaker economy could close small businesses at higher rates, shrink card volumes and slow spending on software, and the company says fixed and semi-fixed costs including debt service cannot be cut quickly; interest-rate rises matter through the floating-rate term loan. Payment-network rules, data-privacy law and AI regulation raise compliance cost but are not quantified in the filings, and international revenue is 11.21% of the first half, so currency is minor.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C08

The credit-translated SWOT is as follows. Strengths are dispersed recurring revenue, a stable gross margin, a long simple capital structure and positive free cash flow. Weaknesses are slipping retention, add-back-heavy earnings, a persistent control weakness and repurchases above free cash flow after amortization. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are payments cross-selling and AI products raising revenue per customer, remediation of the control weakness and holding repurchases inside free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are a small-business downturn, price competition from low-barrier entrants, rising rates after the swaps expire and a sponsor sell-down or disorderly chief executive change.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C07
### Outlook

Over 12 to 24 months the issuer's own guidance and the swap expiry set the picture. Management expects results toward the lower end of ranges that were unchanged since March, quarterly results have so far met or beaten their ranges, and no maturity falls due beyond USD 5.50 million of amortization a year; headwinds are retention near 94%, spending that outruns revenue, the dilutive ZyraTalk purchase and the October 2027 swap expiry. A hearing on the sponsors' chief executive approval right was scheduled for October 19, 2026 and its outcome is not in the sources.

Basis: calculation C02; calculation C09; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

Over three to five years the question is refinancing. The revolver matures in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031, so the 2029 and 2030 results decide the terms of a refinancing of about USD 523.88 million of principal; sector tailwinds are small-business demand for vertical software and digital payments, and sector headwinds are small-business failures, competitive entry and consolidation of customers, which can bring fee pressure.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside begins with the customer base, not a lender event. A soft economy closes small businesses and cuts card volumes while retention, already near 94%, slips further and contracts end on 30 days' notice, so revenue growth stalls; because spending is rising 10.67% and rent, salaries and debt service are semi-fixed, EBITDA falls faster than revenue. Each USD 10.0 million of lost last-twelve-month reported EBITDA lifts gross leverage from 4.22x to 4.59x and lowers reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.43x, and the pressure compounds if floating-rate cost rises after October 2027.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58

Liquidity would absorb the shock before covenants or maturities matter. With free cash flow of USD 71.69 million and cash of USD 133.50 million, only a revolver draw above 35% of commitments, which is USD 43.75 million, would start the first lien leverage test of 7.50x; with zero operating cash flow, cash alone would meet cash interest and amortization for 3.46 years and cash plus the full revolver, if it stayed available, for 6.70 years. The levers are suspending buybacks of USD 82.11 million a year, slowing spending by about USD 7.42 million per half-year and capitalized software of USD 15.58 million per half-year, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within two years; the exposure is the 2030 to 2031 refinancing if EBITDA is lower by then.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52
### Overall credit view

Overall, EverCommerce presents an adequate business profile supported by dispersed recurring revenue and a stable gross margin, but credit quality is constrained by slowing growth, add-back-heavy earnings and sponsor-controlled governance with a weak reporting record. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers scheduled amortization 13.03x, although it does not cover buybacks on top. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilizing before the revolver matures in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031, and on lenders' continued appetite. The primary downside path is weaker retention and spending that outruns revenue pressing EBITDA and leverage while repurchases continue. The profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set was supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer benchmarks and the filings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Top risk: retention-led earnings erosion ahead of a 2031 bullet refinancing.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
